rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The map is sourced only from the captured snapshot; all anomalies found while tracing the backbone are retained as open_details instead of being asserted as defects. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

question.question: When a replica receives PreAccept for instance (Replica, Instance) while its local record for that instance already has Status >= ACCEPTED but stores no commands, handlePreAccept writes the received command into InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] instead of the addressed instance InstanceSpace[preAccept.Replica][Instance]. Is any legal history able to put a replica in that state with preAccept.LeaderId != preAccept.Replica, and if so does the addressed record (Replica, Instance) stay without commands (halting its row's execution and the recovery replies about it) while an unrelated record (LeaderId, Instance) acquires a command that no quorum committed for it?
question.importance: Wrong-slot attribution of a command mutates protocol state without any quorum behind it: a record that never committed that command can become executable as though it had, while the record the message was addressed to can be left permanently unexecutable because executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and findSCC returns false for a command-less instance. Both effects are consensus-visible (an uncommitted command can reach the state machine, and a committed instance can stop making progress).
contexts: instance owned by replica R and led by replica L != R (recovery re-proposal)
instance owned and led by the same replica (normal proposal) as the control that must behave identically
event_paths: deliver PreAccept(LeaderId=L, Replica=R, Instance=i, Ballot=b, Command=c, Seq, Deps) to a replica whose InstanceSpace[R][i] has Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil
compare the record that receives Cmds after the handler returns against the record named by (Replica, Instance)

supporting_behavior_ids.B5-slow-path-accept: shows that the accept phase stores accepted attributes on followers without any status transition, which is the premise the >= ACCEPTED branch would need
supporting_behavior_ids.B11-prepare-resolution: re-runs pre-accept on behalf of another replica's instance, which is the only read path in which PreAccept.LeaderId differs from PreAccept.Replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B12-try-preaccept: another recovery path that re-sends a command for an instance owned by a different replica
supporting_behavior_ids.B7-execute-scheduler: shows the execution requirement Cmds != nil that makes a command-less record of the addressed instance a permanent row stall

counterevidence: no read path found so far sets Status >= ACCEPTED together with Cmds == nil on a replica that did not already hold the command: leader-side transitions copy lb.cmds, handleCommit copies commit.Command, and a nil Command does not survive the wire format as nil (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit)
handleAccept deliberately stores accepted attributes without a status transition, which would make the branch unreachable for acceptors rather than wrong (S11-handleAccept)
unknowns: whether any in-repository path (for example a recovery that commits an instance for which no replica reported a command) can leave Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil at a replica
whether the branch was intended to address the instance owner and the LeaderId index is the only wrong part, or whether the accepted-state condition is also wrong
whether an executor can observe the wrong-slot write, since executeCommands requires Cmds != nil and Status == COMMITTED for the affected record
question.trigger_rationale: Source reading showed the discrepancy directly: S9-handlePreAccept uses preAccept.Replica at lines 782, 792-798, 810, 816 and 828-829, but preAccept.LeaderId at line 809 for the same object. The state needed to reach the branch (Status >= ACCEPTED with nil Cmds on a replica receiving a PreAccept) is not obviously produced by any path read so far: handleAccept stores bal/vbal/Seq/Deps without recording ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept), the leader-side ACCEPTED/COMMITTED transitions set Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply), handleCommit installs commit.Command (S13-handleCommit), and a marshalled nil command slice comes back as a non-nil empty slice. The Candidate therefore fixes the reachability premise as the discriminator rather than assuming the defect is triggered.
